question: The new ₹20 note announced by the Reserve Bank of India in May 2025 is part of _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series** was introduced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in **November 2016** after the demonetization of ₹500 and ₹1000 notes.
 
• This series features **enhanced security features** such as micro-lettering, intaglio printing, and a color-shifting security thread to ensure counterfeit deterrence.
 
• Each denomination in the series has a unique color scheme and motif that reflects **India’s cultural heritage**. For instance, the ₹20 note in the Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series features the motif of **Ellora Caves** on the reverse side.
 
• The front side of the note features a portrait of **Mahatma Gandhi**, the RBI emblem, and other security elements like watermark and electrotype.
 
• The size and dimensions of the notes under this series vary for each denomination, making them user-friendly for visually impaired individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav Series:**

 
 
• This series does not exist as of now. It is a hypothetical option included in the question.
 
• The term "**Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav**" refers to the celebration of **75 years of Indian Independence**, but no specific currency series has been launched under this name.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi Heritage Series:**
 
 
• The Gandhi Heritage Series pertains to **special commemorative coins and stamps** launched by the Government of India to honor Mahatma Gandhi’s legacy.
 
• This series is **not related to the issuance of banknotes**.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi (Old) Series:**
 
 
• This series was introduced in **1996** and remained in circulation until the introduction of the Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series in 2016.
 
• It included denominations such as ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹500, and ₹1000, all featuring **Mahatma Gandhi’s portrait**.
 
• The series lacked advanced security features compared to the New Series and was phased out gradually.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ellora Caves:**

 
 
• Located in the state of **Maharashtra**, the Ellora Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The caves are renowned for their **rock-cut architecture**, representing three major religions: Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism.
 
• The motif of Ellora Caves on the ₹20 note highlights India’s rich cultural and historical heritage.
 
 
 
• **Security Features in Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series:**
 
 
• Color-shifting security thread to prevent counterfeiting.
 
• Micro-lettering of denomination for enhanced authentication.
 
• Raised printing for visually impaired individuals.
 
• Watermark of Mahatma Gandhi and electrotype numeral for easy identification.
 
 
 
• **Introduction Timeline:**
 
 
• ₹500 and ₹2000 notes in the Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series were the first denominations introduced during **demonetization in November 2016**.
 
• Other denominations like ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, and ₹100 were gradually introduced in subsequent years.
